note: Bungie's code ends where the Xbox SDK's D3DX zlib code begins: compress2 at 0x2cb510, then uncompress, deflateInit2_ and deflateReset, which d3dx8.lib defines (compress.obj, uncompr.obj, deflate.obj). Retail builds them with register conventions, so the library signatures miss them. The last game function is 0x2cb4e2; everything from 0x2cb510 up in .text is libraries and third-party code.

ranges.note: Havok's pool memory methods, found by decompiling: they build without link-time code generation (/GL-) and are reached only through the allocator's vtable. The allocator's other functions around them (0x22c390-0x22c71f, 0x22cb00-0x22cbc0) build with it and use the game's register conventions, so they are the game's.

Havok, found by decompiling. Its matched functions all build without link-time code generation (/GL-), as few of the game's do, and use the standard calling conventions where the game's use registers; C++ exception frames, which no game function has, belong to its functions; and its rows call, are called by and share data with each other. The ranges leave out the import thunks at 0x2d6f84-0x2d6fa1, the jump into game code at 0x2d6fb0, two library signature hits (0x2d8d80 and 0x319740) and 0x313320, which game code calls.
